course_description:
This is an upper-advanced level capstone course designed for students who have completed JAPN3102 or equivalent. The course aims to enhance students’ language proficiency and cultural competence. Through project-based learning, students will engage with real-world issues in Japanese-speaking contexts and apply their linguistic and cultural knowledge to explore and solve problems. The course encourages critical thinking and intercultural reflection. It culminates in a final project that showcases both personal and academic growth, helping students prepare for future studies, professional opportunities, or intercultural engagement.

This course introduces the fundamental analytical tools used in linguistics for the analysis of the Japanese language. It explores specific areas of grammar that exhibit pervasive structural and semantic differences between Japanese and English. The interplay between socio-cultural factors and language use will also be discussed. The course will assist students in systematisingﾠand consolidating theirﾠknowledge of Japanese to further your proficiency.ﾠ

course_aims: This course aims to strengthen students’ advanced proficiency in Japanese and enhance their intercultural understanding. The course helps students develop their ability to critically analyse linguistic and cultural issues in Japanese-speaking contexts and apply their knowledge to real-world challenges.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse variation in Japanese language use and the diversity of its users across social, regional, and cultural contexts.
Communicate appropriately in Japanese with diverse users by applying knowledge of linguistic variation and sociocultural norms (e.g., formality, age, region).
Collaborate with a partner or group to produce spoken and written work in Japanese.
Apply cultural knowledge and context-sensitive analysis to propose effective responses to current cross-cultural challenges.

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Worksheets will be distributed in hard copy in Tutorial 1. Students are required to work on the worksheet in class as a part of class activities, and then take them home to review, edit and complete by the specified due date.
The worksheets will be also available on Blackboard in the assessment folder, for students to download and complete independently if they miss class. Students must handwrite the answers on worksheets in Japanese using pens, pencils, and erasers.
Upon completion, they should scan the required pages in the portrait direction (e.g., using the Scanner app or scanner) and upload the scanned document in PDF format to the appropriate link in the “Worksheets” folder in the Assessment section of Blackboard. Worksheets that are typed rather than handwritten do not meet the assessment requirements.
There will be 8 worksheets available throughout the semester. However, please note that only the top 6 marks will count towards the students' grades . This means that students can miss 2 submissions without lowering their marks.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
Extensions are not available for these worksheet tasks. The worksheets are designed to support ongoing engagement with scheduled class activities, and feedback and/or answers are provided during class.
There are 8 worksheets across the semester, with only the student's best 6 results contributing to the final assessment mark. This design provides flexibility for students who are unable to complete up to two worksheets due to occasional absences or unforeseen circumstances, without adversely affecting their overall mark for this assessment.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.

assessment_details.title: Intercultural Scenario Analysis
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, AI Required. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment task, students will analyse and respond to intercultural communication scenarios presented in Japanese. Drawing on relevant course concepts and intercultural frameworks, students will identify and evaluate factors that contribute to communication challenges, consider alternative interpretations and responses, and justify contextually appropriate courses of action. The task incorporates the critical evaluation of AI-generated content as one source of perspectives and interpretations. Students will demonstrate their ability to communicate and justify their analyses in Japanese while reflecting on the opportunities and limitations of different approaches to intercultural communication. The assessment is designed to develop students’ linguistic proficiency, intercultural understanding, critical thinking, and reflective judgement. A Generative AI Use Declaration must be submitted as a part of the assessment, documenting any use of AI tools in the development of the work. The examination will be completed on paper and assesses students’ understanding of the key concepts, terminology, and communication skills developed throughout Weeks 1–10 of the course. The examination may include multiple-choice questions, short-answer questions, and tasks requiring students to apply course concepts to intercultural communication scenarios. The exam will be hand-written, and no dictionaries or electronic devices are allowed. Use of AI in this assessment: This assessment task is to be completed in-person. assessment_details.title: Intercultural Communication Project
assessment_details.due_date: 13/11/2026 3:00 pm Friday, EXAM WEEK 1 Submitted via Blackboard
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment, students will prepare a narrated PowerPoint presentation in Japanese based on a case involving intercultural communication. Drawing on concepts and frameworks introduced in the course, students will analyse an instance of intercultural conflict, misunderstanding, or communication challenge, identify the cultural norms, values, and assumptions that contribute to the interaction, and propose culturally informed responses or solutions. Students will demonstrate their ability to apply intercultural concepts to real-world situations, communicate complex ideas in Japanese, and justify their analyses and recommendations using evidence and course content. The presentation should integrate description, analysis, proposed solutions, and critical reflection on the broader implications of intercultural communication. A Generative AI Use Declaration must be submitted as a part of the assessment documenting any use of AI tools in the development of the work.
